chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Umar ibn al-Khattab was brought a slave girl against whom they had testified that she had committed adultery. And part of her story was that she was an orphan with a man, and the man used to be frequently absent from his family. So the orphan girl matured, and the wife feared that her husband might marry her. So she called women until they restrained her, and she took her virginity with her finger. So when her husband returned from his absence, the wife accused the orphan girl of immorality and established proof from her neighbors who had aided her in doing so.

That was raised to Umar, but he did not know how to judge regarding her. Then he said to the man, 'Go to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and we will go with you to him.' So they came to Ali (peace be upon him) and related the story to him. He said to the wife of the man, 'Do you have proof or evidence?' She said, 'There are witnesses for me, these neighbors of mine who testify against her with what I am saying,' so she presented them.

So Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) brought out the sword from its sheath and placed it in front of him, and ordered that each one of them enter a room. Then he called the wife of the man and interrogated her from every aspect, but she refused to waver from her words. So he returned her to the room in which she was, and called one of the witnesses, and sat on his knees. Then he said, 'Do you recognize me? I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, and this is my sword. The wife of the man has said what she said. If you return to the truth, I will give you amnesty; and if you are not truthful to me, I will fill the sword with your blood.' So she turned to Umar and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! The amnesty is for me.' So the Commander of the Faithful said to her, 'So speak the truth.'

She said, 'No, by Allah, except that she saw beauty and a good figure in her, so she feared the ruin of her husband upon her. So she gave her an intoxicating drink, and called us, so we restrained her, and she deflowered her with her finger.'
So Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah is the Greatest! I am the first to differentiate between the two witnesses, except for Daniel the Prophet.'

So Ali necessitated upon the woman the legal penalty of the slanderer, and necessitated upon all of them together the dower, and made her dower to be four hundred dirhams. And he ordered that the woman be separated from the man, and her husband divorce her, and he married the girl to him, and Ali (peace be upon him) paid the dower from himself.

So Umar said, 'O Abu al-Hasan! Narrate to us the story of Daniel.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, Daniel was an orphan, having no mother for him nor a father, and a woman from the Children of Israel, an old woman, took him in and raised him.'

And a king from the kings of the Children of Israel had two judges for him, and they had a friend who was a righteous man, and he had a beautiful, lovely wife, and he used to come to the king and discuss with him.

And the king had a need to send a man in one of his matters, so he said to the two judges, 'Choose a man to send him in one of my matters.' So they said, 'So and so.' So the king sent him. So the man said to the two judges, 'I bequeath to you both regarding my wife for her safety.' So they said, 'Yes.' So the man went out.

So the two judges used to come to the door of the friend, so they desired his wife and enticed her to give herself to them, but she refused. So they said to her, 'By Allah, if you do not do it, we will testify against you in the presence of the king with adultery, then we will have you stoned.' So she said, 'Do whatever you both like.' So they went to the king and informed him, and testified in his presence that she had committed adultery. So a great matter entered the king because of that, and his grief over her intensified, and he was admiring her.

So he said to them, 'Your words are accepted, but stone her after three days.' And he called out in the city in which he was, 'Attend the killing of so-and-so the worshipper, for she has committed adultery, for the two judges have testified against her with that.' So the people were many regarding that, and the king said to his vizier, 'What do you have regarding this from a stratagem?' He said, 'I have nothing regarding that.'

So the vizier went out on the third day, and it was the last of her days, and he saw naked boys playing, and among them was Daniel, and he did not know him. So Daniel said, 'O group of children! Come, until I am the king, and you be so-and-so the worshipper, and so-and-so and so-and-so be the two judges testifying against her.'

Then he gathered dust and made a sword from a reed, and said to the boys, 'Take this one by the hand and move him to such and such a place, and take this one by the hand and move him to such and such a place.'

Then he called one of them and said to him, 'Speak the truth, for if you do not speak the truth, I will kill you.' And the vizier was standing, watching and listening. So he said, 'I testify that she committed adultery.' He said, 'When?' He said, 'On such and such a day.' He said, 'Return him to his place and bring the other one.' So they returned him to his place and brought the other one. So he said to him, 'With what do you testify?' He said, 'I testify that she committed adultery.' He said, 'When?' He said, 'On such and such a day.' He said, 'With whom?' He said, 'With so-and-so, son of so-and-so.' He said, 'And where?' He said, 'At such and such a place.'

So one of them contradicted his companion. So Daniel said, 'Allah is the Greatest! They testified with falsehood. O so-and-so, call out among the people that these two testified against so-and-so with falsehood, so present them and kill them.' So the vizier went to the king quickly and informed him of the news. So the king sent for the two judges, and they differed just as the two boys had differed. So the king called out among the people and ordered with their killing.

key_terms.حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ: The legal penalty for the slanderer

ai.seo_question: How did Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) use witness examination to prove a false adultery accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Ali ibn Abi Talib’s judicial acumen in distinguishing between true and false witnesses (*al-farq bayn al-shahidayn*) by exposing the mistress's fabrication of the girl's virginity to prevent her marriage. Ali explicitly links his method to the Prophet Daniel’s (*Dhaniel*) use of children to uncover discrepancies in testimony, establishing a precedent for using psychological insight in legal proceedings. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the infallible Imam’s ability to discern truth through divine inspiration and logical deduction.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

They came to Umar Bin Al-Khattab with a slave girl who had been testified against that she had committed adultery, and from her story was that she was an orphan (in the custody of) a man, and the man used to be frequently absent from his family. So the orphan girl matured, so the wife (of that man) feared that her husband may marry her. So she called women (friends) until they restrained her. So she took away her virginity by her fingers. So when the husband returned from his absence, the wife accused the orphan girl with the immorality, and established the proof from her neighbours who had aided her upon that.

So that was raised to Umar, but he did not know how to judge with regards to it. Then he said to the man, ‘Go to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and we will go with you to him<sup>asws</sup>’. So they came over to Ali<sup>asws</sup> and related to him<sup>asws</sup> the story. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to the wife of the man, ‘Is there any proof for you, or evidence?’ She said, ‘There are witnesses for me, these neighbours of mine who are testifying against her with what I am saying, so I am presenting them.

So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> brought out the sword from its sheath, so he<sup>asws</sup> placed it in front of him, and ordered for each one of them (women witnesses) to enter into a room. Then he called the wife of the man, so he<sup>asws</sup> interrogated her with every aspect, but she refused to waver from her words. So he returned her to the room in which she was, and called for one of the witnesses, and sat upon his<sup>asws</sup> knees. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you recognise me<sup>asws</sup>? I<sup>asws</sup> am Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and this is my<sup>asws</sup> sword, and the wife of the man has said what she said, and returned to the truth, and I<sup>asws</sup> gave her amnesty, and if you are not truthful to me, I<sup>asws</sup> will fill the sword from you (your blood)’. So she turned around to Umar and said, ‘O commander of the faithful! The amnesty for me’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to her: ‘So speak the truth to me<sup>asws</sup>’.

So she said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, except that she saw the (in the orphan girl) beauty and body, so she feared mischief of her husband upon her, so she gave her an intoxicating drink, and called us over, so we restrained her, and she deflowered her with her fingers’.

So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj </sup>is the Greatest! I<sup>asws</sup> am the first one to differentiate between two witnesses, except for Dainel<sup>as</sup>, the Prophet<sup>asws</sup>.

So Aliasws necessitated upon the woman the legal penalty (Hadd) of the slanderer, and necessitated upon all the women together, the dower, and made her dower to be four hundred Dirhams, and ordered the woman that be denied from the man and divorced her, and married the girl to him, and Aliasws paid (contributed) the dower from himselfasws’.

So Umar said, ‘O Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup>! So narrate to us with a Hadeeth of Daniel<sup>as</sup>’. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Dainel<sup>as</sup> was an orphan, not having a mother for him<sup>as</sup> nor a father, and a woman from the Children of Israel, very old, cared for him<sup>asws</sup> and loved him<sup>as</sup>.

And (there was a) a king from the kings of the Children of Israel who had two judges for him who had a friend who was a righteous man, for whom was a woman with a beautiful body, and he used to come to the king and discuss with him.

And the king had a need from that man, to send him regarding one of his matters. So he said to the two judges, ‘Both of you choose a man to send him in one of my matters’. So they both said, ‘So and so’. So the king diverted himself to him. So the man said to the two judges, ‘I bequeath to both of you with my wife for her safety’. So they both said, ‘Yes’. So the man went out.

So the judges used to come to the door of the friend, so they both desired his wife, but she repulsed them both from herself and refused. So they both said to her, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If you were not to do it, we would testify against you in the presence of the king with the adultery, then we would have you stoned’. So she said, ‘So do whatever you both like to’. So they both went over to the king and informed him, and testified in his presence that she is an adulteress. So there entered a grievous matter into the king due to that, and his grief got aggravated by it, and he had also admired her.

So he said to them both, ‘Both your words are accepted, but, stone her after three days’. He called out in the city in which he (her husband) was, for (the people) to be present for the killing of so and so woman worshipper, for she had committed adultery, for the two judges has testified against her’. So there were a lot of people with regards to that, and the king said to his Vizier, ‘What is with you with regards to this from an excuse?’ So he said, ‘There is nothing with me regarding that anything’.

So the Vizier went out on the third day, and it was the last of her days, and there were (some) little boys playing, and among them was Dainel<sup>as</sup>, and he did not know him<sup>as</sup>. So Daniel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O group of children! Come, until I<sup>as</sup> become (pretend) I<sup>as</sup> am the king, and you become the so and so worshipper woman, and so and so, and so and so become the two judges testifying against her.

Then he<sup>as</sup> gathered dust and made a sword from a stick, and said to the children: ‘Take this (pretend judge) by your hand and go to this such and such a place, and take the hand of this (the other pretend judge) and go to this such and such a place.

Then he<sup>as</sup> called one of the two and said to him: ‘Speak the truth. If you do not speak the truth, I<sup>as</sup> will kill you’. And the Vizier was standing and listening’. So he (one pretend judge said) said, ‘I testify that she has committed adultery’. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘When?’ He said, ‘On such and such a day’. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Return him to his place and bring the other one’. So he returned him to his place, and came with the other one. So he<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘With what do you testify?’ So he said, ‘I testify that she has committed adultery’. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘When?’ He said, ‘On such and such a day’. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘With whom?’ He said, ‘With so and so, son of so and so’. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘And where?’ He said, ‘At such and such a place’.

So one of the two contradicted his companions. So Daniel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest! A false testimony. O so and so, call out among the people that these two have testified against so and so woman with falsity, therefore present them and kill both of them’. So the Vizier went to the king quickly and informed him of the news. So the king sent for the two judges, and they both differed just as the two boys had differed. So the king called out among the people, and ordered with the killing of them both’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘ Abd Allah ibn ‘Uthman from a man who has narrated the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that in the time of the government of Ali, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, a man from the mountains with his slave went for al-Hajj. His slave committed a sin and his master beat him as a measure for discipline. He (the slave) said, ‘You are not my master. I am your master.’ They continued threatening each other. He told him, ‘Wait until our arrival in al-Kufah, O enemy of Allah, and I will take you before Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’

When they arrived in al-Kufah, they came to ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and the one who had beaten the slave said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, this is my slave. He committed a sin and I beat him for discipline but he jumped on me.’ The other one said, ‘He by Allah is my slave. My father sent him for me for guidance but he jumped on me to claim and take away my assets.’ They each began to swear and the other to refute. He (the Imam) told them to leave for the night, be truthful and come to me with the truth.

The next day ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked Qanbar to make two holes in the wall. He (the Imam) said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the morning would remain reciting prayer after his morning Salat (prayer) until the sun would rise by the length of a spear. The two men then came and people gathered. They said that there is a case like no other case before him (the Imam), it is difficult and he (the Imam) may not be able to solve it. He (the Imam) then asked them, ‘What do you say?’ Each one swore and claimed that the other man is his slave. He (the Imam) then told them, ‘You both stand up. I do not think you are speaking the truth.’

He then told one of them to place his neck in the hole in the wall and pull out his head from the other side. Then he told the other one to do the same thing. He (the Imam) said, ‘O Qanbar, bring for me the sword of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, quickly and of the two strike down the neck of the slave one.’

He (the Imam) said that the slave quickly pulled his head out of the hole. Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked him (slave), ‘Did you not think that you were not a slave?’ The other one remained with his head in the hole. He then said, ‘Yes, but he beat me up and transgressed against me.’
He (the Imam) said that ’Amir al- Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, prepared a document for him and handed over the slave to him (the slave-master).”’
